I'll flag this accordingly.

Published online:
    ~Early September 2023 (exact date not stated in article; inferred from internal context)

Geographic focus:
    Hawaii, Central North Pacific Ocean (USA)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report YES (references Iniki 1992, 155-year records)
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) YES (remainder of hurricane season, El Niño strengthening)
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) YES (climate crisis compounding future storm intensity)

Synopsis:
    Two named storms (Lala in August, Lowell in September 2023) struck Hawaii in the same season — an unusual occurrence for islands historically shielded by cool Pacific waters. The article attributes this to El Niño-driven warm sea surface temperatures pushing storm tracks westward toward the islands, layered on top of human-caused climate change. Lowell briefly reached Category 5, causing significant infrastructure damage on Kauai. Forecasters warn the season is not over, El Niño is expected to intensify further, and the combined effect of El Niño and climate change is projected to produce stronger, wetter Pacific storms going forward.
